query: If the most common operational burdens described in the text were eliminated, how much would resolution duration drop?

per_column.name: incident_category
per_column.rationale: Categorizes the operational burden type described in text; the query targets eliminating 'operational burdens', so this is the treatment lever, though category itself is more a descriptor than a settable action.

per_column.name: failure_type
per_column.rationale: Represents the kind of failure/burden described; aligns with the 'operational burdens' to be eliminated. Borderline intervenable — it is a diagnosed condition rather than a lever an actor sets.

per_column.name: affected_system_scope
per_column.rationale: System scope (server_side, infrastructure) plausibly influences both the type of burden and the resolution time; a common cause not named in the query.

per_column.name: reassignment_indicator
per_column.rationale: Reassignment typically occurs on the path between the burden/incident and the duration outcome, so it is a mediator, not a confounder.

per_column.name: recurrence_signal
per_column.rationale: Recurrence could drive both the nature of the burden and duration; near-degenerate (496/4) so weak, but conceptually a common cause not named.

per_column.name: scope_indicator
per_column.rationale: Whether an issue is individual vs system_wide can affect both burden type and duration; a plausible common cause not named.

per_column.name: time_of_day_band
per_column.rationale: Time incident occurs (after_hours/overnight) affects staffing/response and correlates with incident type; a pre-treatment common cause not named in query.

per_column.name: assigned_agent
per_column.rationale: Agent assignment could be argued as mediator, but agent skill/experience is a common cause of both handling and duration; treated as a confounder not named. Assignment is itself intervenable.

per_column.name: caller_segment
per_column.rationale: Caller identity/segment can influence both the kind of issue reported and resolution time; a common cause not named in the query.

judge.rationale: The query asks an interventional what-if: eliminate the most common operational burdens and estimate the drop in resolution duration. The added columns identify the treatment via incident_category/failure_type, but these encode a diagnosed condition (an intrinsic classification of what went wrong) rather than a lever an actor can SET, CHANGE, or DECIDE — you cannot straightforwardly 'set' a connectivity_failure to none as an operational intervention. Thus the intervenability requirement (a) is not clearly satisfied. On confounders (b), the set does include several plausible pre-treatment common causes NOT named in the query — affected_system_scope, scope_indicator, time_of_day_band, caller_segment — which is the capability under test and earns partial credit. However quality is diluted by a mediator misclassified as a covariate (reassignment_indicator), a near-degenerate signal (recurrence_signal, 496/4), and assigned_agent which sits ambiguously between mediator and confounder. Overall: treatment present but weakly intervenable; moderate, mixed-quality confounder coverage.
